title: Conditioning Memory Tests of Drosophila melanogaster with and without Predators
author: Krams, Indrikis
license_note: Zenodo record metadata license field: cc-by-4.0

steps.title: Collect and age flies
steps.instruction: Gather 10 adult male Drosophila melanogaster that have been raised under standard conditions and are 6–7 days old.

steps.title: Prepare odorant solutions
steps.instruction: Dilute 3‑octanol and 4‑methylcyclohexanol each to a concentration of 0.6 mL per litre of paraffin.

steps.title: Set up conditioning apparatus
steps.instruction: Arrange a test‑tube shaker (Heidolph Instruments, Schwabach, Germany) capable of delivering 2000 rpm vibration pulses of 1 s duration every 5 s, and a T‑maze for later memory testing.

steps.title: Perform spaced conditioning training
steps.instruction: Run five training sessions separated by 20‑minute intervals. For each session:

substeps.instruction: Expose the flies for 30 s to one odorant (randomly chosen per group) while delivering mechanical shock pulses at 2000 rpm, 1 s each, every 5 s.
Allow a 60 s rest period with no odor and no shock.
Expose the flies for 30 s to the other odorant without any shock.
Allow a second 60 s rest period.

steps.title: Conduct memory retention assays
steps.instruction: Test flies at 1 hour (short‑term memory) and 24 hours (long‑term memory) after the final (5th) training session.

substeps.instruction: Place flies at the entry of a T‑maze.
Deliver two converging air streams, one carrying 3‑octanol and the other 4‑methylcyclohexanol.
Allow flies to choose between the two odors for 60 s.

steps.title: Calculate memory score
steps.instruction: Compute the memory score as the difference in the proportion of flies choosing 3‑octanol between the group conditioned to avoid 4‑methylcyclohexanol and the group conditioned to avoid 3‑octanol.
